title: Knee Surgery Rules Sinner Out of the Australian Open
summary:
Jannik Sinner will not play at the Australian Open in January. The 25-year-old Italian tennis star has had surgery on his knee, and Tennis Australia has confirmed he will miss the tournament in Melbourne. Sinner said in a social media post on Tuesday that he had an operation to improve the condition of his iliotibial band, a thick band of tissue that runs along the outside of the knee. Tennis Australia chief executive Andrew Abdo said the two sides had been in regular touch. "Jannik loves competing here in Melbourne and is looking forward to returning for AO 2028," Abdo said. "We wish him all the very best with his recovery and look forward to seeing him back on court soon."

It is a big blow for the tournament. Sinner won the Australian Open in both 2024 and 2025, and he has not played competitively since winning Wimbledon on 12 July. The main draw of the 2027 Australian Open starts on 17 January. In the 2026 tournament, his run ended in a five-set semi-final defeat by Novak Djokovic.

Sinner was the dominant player of the first half of the season, winning 44 of his singles matches and losing just three. He won five Masters 1000 titles in a row between March and May, becoming the youngest man to complete the "career Golden Masters", and he reclaimed the world's top ranking from Alcaraz along the way. Then came a shock second-round exit at the French Open, where Zverev went on to win his first Grand Slam title.

Sinner bounced back on grass, beating Djokovic in the Wimbledon semi-finals before coming back from a set down to beat Zverev in the final. He ended his season in early October, so he could not defend the points he had won with titles in China, Vienna, Paris and at the ATP Finals at the end of 2025. Zverev went on to win the US Open and finish the year as world number one. Now Sinner's focus turns to getting healthy.
why_it_matters: Star players shape the biggest tournaments, so an injury to a two-time champion changes the Australian Open for fans and for the other players chasing the title.

background_read: The Australian Open is one of the biggest tennis tournaments in the world, played each year in Melbourne.
Top players build their whole season around the Grand Slam tournaments, so missing one can change a player's year.
Knee injuries are common in tennis because players run, stop, and turn hard on the court, and surgery can mean months away from playing.
When a star player is out, the tournament loses one of its biggest draws, but other players get a new chance to go further.
